chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Dāwūd al-Mustariqq, from ʿAlī ibn Maymūn, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Three people—Allah will not look toward them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: one who claims an Imamate from Allah that does not belong to him; one who denies an Imam from Allah; and one who alleges that both of them have a share in Islam.

key_terms.إِمَامَةً: the office of divinely appointed leadership and authority
key_terms.عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ: a painful punishment in the hereafter
key_terms.نَصِيبًا: a share, portion, or claim of legitimacy
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when final judgment occurs
key_terms.يُزَكِّيهِمْ: purify them or declare them cleansed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about falsely claiming or denying the divinely appointed Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns three grave deviations concerning the divinely appointed Imamate: falsely claiming it, rejecting a true Imam, and giving equal legitimacy to both truth and falsehood in this matter. It emphasizes that such positions bring severe consequences in the hereafter and presents Imamate as a matter of divine designation rather than human claim.
